To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the majority of minute gastric differentiated carcinomas (DAs) have a gastric phenotype.

the gastric phenotype is the most frequent, the incidence of gastric phenotype tends to decrease as the tumor diameter increases, and the surrounding intestinal metaplasias are immature and incomplete in the gastric phenotype.

gastric differentiated adenocarinoma with gastric phenotype may histogenetically develop from the gastric proper gland without intestinal metaplisia and that gastric differentiated adenoma with gastric phenotype changes to intestinal type phenotypically as the tumor grows.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the histogenetic relationship between gastric gland proper, intestinal metaplaia and DA.
the phenotypic expression and its histogenesis in minute gastric differentiated adenoma and DA.
the histogenetic mechanism of DA and its relation to the progression of intestinal metaplasias.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DA with gastric phenotype has a different histogenetic background from that of DA with intestinal phenotype.
DA with gastric phenotype may be derived from the gland proper, whereas DA with gastric–intestional or intestinal phenotype may be derived mainly from the intestinal metaplasic epithelium.
DA with gastric phenotype may be a precursor of DA with intestinal type phenotype.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the histogenesis of DA is not simple, but rather a complicated process involving various types of phenotypic expressions.
gastric type DA is derived from the gastric glands proper and intestinal type DA is derived mainly from the gastric glands with intestinal metaplasis.
DA with gastric phenotype may have two pathways of carcinogenesis, i.e. one from the gastric gland and one from the intestinal metaplasic epithelium.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the gastric phenotype is a common histologic feature of minute differentiated adenocarcincinoma of the stomach, and that the gastric–intestinal phenotype may be a transition from the gastric phenotype.
DA with gastric phenotype can be histogenetically derived directly from the gastric mucosal gland proper.
the gastric type DA is the most prevalent type of gastric differentiated adenocarconoma, followed by intestinal and gastric‐intestinal type.
